Analog Output Monitor Selection
The operation status of motor can be displayed as analog voltage, such as speed and current. This servo drive provides 2 output channels, MON1 (Y) and MON2 (X). This signal is based on the power ground.
The max output voltage (Max.Volt) can be configured to either 8 V or 10 V by ID266(P2.112).bit0.

See Analog Monitoring in the user manual.

Y (MON1) and X (MON2)
0=Motor speed (±Max.Volt V/Max. speed)
1=Motor torque (±Max.Volt V/Max. torque)
2=Pulse command frequency (+Max.Volt V/4.5Mpps)
3=Speed command (±Max.Volt V/Max. speed command)
4=Torque command (±Max.Volt V/Max. torque command)
5=VBUS voltage (±Max.Volt V/450 V)
6=ID181(P1.101) mV
7=ID182(P1.102) mV
UZ Reserved

Low-frequency Vibration Suppression Mode Setting
When the value is set to 1, the drive is in automatic mode for vibration suppression. When vibration cannot be detected or the vibration frequency is stable, the parameter is reset to 0 and the frequency for vibration suppression is automatically saved to ID135 (P1.025).

0=Disable auto low frequency vibration detection function
1=Disable function automatically after vibration suppression

Low-frequency Vibration Detection Level
When auto suppression is enabled [ID139 (P1.029 = 1)], it automatically searches the vibration frequency. The lower the value is, the more sensitive the detection will be, but it may also easily misjudge noise or regard other low-frequency vibration as frequency to be suppressed. If the value is high, it is less likely to misjudge, but if the vibration frequency of the mechanism is small, it may not detect the frequency of low-frequency vibration.

Zero Speed Window
Sets the range of outputting zero-speed signal (ZSPD). When the forward / reverse speed of the motor is slower than the setting value, the zero-speed signal is set up and the digital output is enabled.

Panel or Software: 0…200
Communication(parameter object): 0…2000

Up to Speed Limit
When the target speed is reached, DO (TSPD) is enabled. When the forward / reverse speed of the motor is faster than the setting value, the target speed is reached and the digital output is enabled.

Encoder Output Resolution
The number of single-phase pulse outputs per revolution; the max. output frequency of the hardware is 19.8 MHz.

Speed Window
When the error between speed command and motor feedback speed is less than this parameter, and after the speed window time ID156 (P1.049), the digital output DO.SP_OK (0x19) is ON.
See DO.SP_OK (Digital Output: speed reached output) in the user manual.

See DO.MC_OK (Digital Output: servo procedure completed) in the user manual.

X: DO output hold option
0=Output status will not hold
1=Output status will hold

Y: Position Offset Alarm
0=E 380 disabled
1=E 380 enabled

In Position Window
In position (PT) mode, when the deviation pulse number is smaller than the In Position Size value, DO.TPOS is on.
In position register (PR) mode, when the deviation between the target position and the actual motor position is smaller than the In Position Size value, DO.TPOS is on.
Rotary motor example: If ID159 (P1.054) = 167772 and the deviation is less than 167772 pulses, which equals 0.01 turns
(167772/16777216 = 0.01), then DO.TPOS is on.

Maximum Speed
Sets the maximum speed of the servo motor.

Overload Warning User Threshold
Determines whether the early warning for overload (DO:OWL) is enabled.
See Description of Digital Output Functions in the user manual.

0…100= If the servo motor continuously outputs a load higher than this value, DO:OWL occurs.

>100= DO:OWL warning is disabled.

Crash Protection Torque Threshold
Sets the protection level as a percentage of rated torque. Setting the value to 0 disables this function.

Crash Protection Filtering Time
If the motor reaches or exceeds the Crash Fault Torque Threshold for longer than the Crash Fault Filtering Time, E 030 (Motor Crash Error) occurs.
This function is only suitable for non-contactable applications, such as electric discharge machines. Set up ID144 (P1.037) LoadInertiaRatio properly.

Friction Compensation
Sets the level of friction compensation as a percentage of rated torque. Setting the value to 0 disables this function.

Friction Compensation Smooth Time Constant
Defines a smoothing constant for friction compensation.

Analog To Position Command Startup Configuration

X: Analog to Position Command Setting
0: Disable
1: Enable
Y: Initial Position Setting
0: Current position is 0V position, motor will move to command position specified by analog input
1: Current position is the command position, motor will not move before the analog input changes

Analog To Position Command Max Rotation Number

Rotation number when the input voltage of analog to position command from 0V to max. (10V). For example, when rotation number is 3 Rev, if the input voltage is 10V, the motor moves +3 rotations. If the input voltage is 5V, the motor moves 1.5 rotations. If the input voltage is -10V, the motor moves -3 rotations.

Auxiliary Feedback Resolution
A/B pulses corresponded to full-closed loop when motor runs a cycle (after quadruple frequency).

Error Limit between Motor and Auxiliary Feedback
If the deviation between the A/B counter of auxiliary feedback and the feedback position of the encoder is greater than this value, fault E 040 (Excessive Deviation of Full Closed-loop Position Control) occurs.

1=Enable full-closed loop function
Y:Selection of OA/OB/OZ output source

1=Encoder of linear scale
2=I/O pulse command
Z: Direction selection of auxiliary feedback
0=Positive direction when A phase leads B phase of auxiliary feedback
1=Positive direction when B phase leads A phase of auxiliary feedback
U: Auxiliary feedback filter function
0=Bypass
1=6.66M
2=1.66M
3=833K
4=416K

When the value is set to 0, the smooth function is disabled.

The compared level for this parameter is the

Power Loss Diagnostic Time
When the disconnection detection protection (UVW) function [ID239 (P2.065) bit 9 = 1] is enabled, this value can determine the response time of the detection mode. Set this value to 0 to apply the servo's default response time.
When not set to 0, the setting should be between 100…800 to set the detection response time.
If speeding up the response time is needed, setting this parameter can help.
When the servo is on and has not started running, set this parameter to detect a disconnection.

When [YX] of ID103 (P0.003) AOMonitorSelection is set to 6, then the analog monitor output voltage be the value of this parameter setting.

Preset Analog Output Value 2
When [YX] of ID103 (P0.003) AOMonitorSelection is set to 7, then the analog monitor output voltage be the value of this parameter setting.

Auxiliary Function
Enables auxiliary functions. Set the value to 0 in normal operation.
0=disable the functions.
1=Switch servo on state
2…4=Reserved
5=Do not retain parameter settings after power-off.
6=Enable command simulation. The DI.SON signal does not work but DO.SRDY is on. Commands are accepted but the motor will not operate.
7=High-speed oscilloscope
8=Back up all parameters to EEPROM and the values remain after cycling power.
-1, -5, -6, -7=Disable functions 1, 5, 6, or 7, respectively
-2…-4, -8=Reserved

Velocity Error Tolerance
In speed mode, this parameter sets the error threshold between the command speed and feedback speed.
If the error is greater than this set value, fault E 007 (Excessive deviation of speed command) occurs.

Position Error Tolerance
In position mode, this parameter sets the error threshold between the command position and feedback position.
If the error is greater than this set value, E 009 (Excessive Deviation of Position Command) occurs.

Resonance Suppression Configuration
Enables or disables (X) auto resonance suppression for each of the 5 notch filters. When disabled, the existing resonance suppression parameter values are fixed. If auto resonance suppression is enabled, you can use auto resonance suppression or manually set the resonance suppression for notch filters 1…4 via (Y) and notch filter 5 via (Z).
See Mechanical Resonance Suppression in the user manual.

Resonance Diagnostic Level
The smaller the parameter value is, the more sensitive the drive is to resonance.

Pulse Clear Mode
Set digital input (DI) as CCLR to enable the Pulse Clear function. If this DI is on, the accumulated position error is reset to 0.

0=CCLR is rising-edge triggered.
1=CCLR is action-level triggered

Bit 0 – 1, Bit 3, Bit 6 – 8, Bit 10 – 15: reserved

Bit 4: Disable A 044 detection (servo function overload warning).

0=Set E 003 as Major Recoverable Fault (have to do the fault reset manually after voltage recovery).
1=Set E 003 as Minor Recoverable Fault (fault is reset automatically after voltage recovery).

Absolute System Setting

X: Operating mode setting
0=Incremental type. An absolute type motor can be operated as an incremental type
1=Absolute type. This setting is only applicable to an absolute type motor. If it is used on an incremental type motor,E 069occurs.
Z: Index coordinates function when an overflow occurs
0=Index coordinates are lost when an overflow occurs.
1=Index coordinates are not affected by overflow, but absolute coordinates are not retained.

1=Pulse

0=PUU
1=Pulse
Bit 2: Overflow warning setting
0=Overflow warning, including A 289 (PUU)
1=No overflow warning
Bit 3 - Bit15: reserved

Position Error Tolerance Time

Position error time is the time during the position error (the deviation of the difference between position command and feedback) exceeds the tolerance error specific by ID219(P2.035).
E 009 (excessive deviation of position command) will be caused when the position error time greater than the time specific by this parameter.

0=FDBK is not latched, FDBK status will not remain when the alarm has been cleared
1=FDBK is latched, FDBK status will remain even when the alarm has been cleared

Bit5: Cancel E 016 IGBT overheat alarm
0=Enable E 016 IGBT overheat alarm
1=Disable E016 IGBT overheat alarm

Torque Threshold to Switch from PI to P
When the torque command exceeds this value, the speed controller gain is switched from PI to P to reduce response overshoot.

Jog Operation
Set the speed for Jog.

There are 3 methods to Jog:
1. Via the panel display
See Jog the Motor without Load in the user manual.
2. Via digital input (DI) control
Using the JOGU and JOGD digital inputs to jog the motor in the positive or negative direction. See Description of Digital Input Functions in the user manual.
3. Via Communication
See Jog the Motor without Load in the user manual.
Set ID215 (P2.030) to 5 when writing via communication, to avoid continually writing the parameters into EEPROM.
